text: I found a hatchet on the beach. I have a feeling I'll need anything and everything that I can get my hands on to survive on this island. I picked it up. Of course, I get shipwrecked on my first exotic getaway. I knew I should've flown. It's okay, at least I have my health -- and a hatchet. What more could I possibly need? Note to self: sarcasm helps.

Waste not, want not. I combed the beach for anything else that may be useful... like a travel agent. Instead, I found a steamer trunk from my ship buried on the beach! That means there could be more things from the ship scattered around the island. Too bad this trunk isn't big enough to ride out of here. My luck it's probably empty, or worse, filled with poisonous snakes.

I put the trunk in my "camp." It's sort of the centerpiece of my furnishings right now. Actually, it's my only furnishing. The steamer trunk will have to wear many hats for the time being. It's the only place I can store my stuff. What stuff? I need some stuff.

I know sea water is off limits, but I seem to remember hearing somewhere that the two basic items necessary to sustain life are coconut milk and... um... something else. Running water? Television? I can't remember. Oh well, coconut milk was the important part. Coconuts aren't half bad, actually, they're pretty good. If only they grew on little bushes, instead of tall trees... or delivered on an extra-large pizza.

There was no reason to wait until I was hungry again to get more coconuts. It made more sense to gather some when I had the energy. Gathering my own food isn't as convenient as a quick trip to the grocery, but you can't beat the price. I have coconuts in the steamer trunk for later when I get the craving for a snack. Perhaps I'll open up a little coconut stand back home with any extras leftover. Wouldn't that be nice... no boss, no deadlines, no schedule. I can see the neon sign blinking now -- "$NeighborLocal:1's Wild Nut Hut."

I'll need more resources, like wood, if I want to make it on this island. I finally used my hatchet to chop some wood -- very empowering! I have to admit all this forced self-reliance is really doing wonders for my confidence. I am going to totally dominate at my next speed-dating event.

I put the "fire" in campfire. You know, dogs are great and all, but fire is truly man's best friend. It's easy to take making fire for granted. I feel like I just split the atom or something. Thank you, Prometheus! Mmm... regenerating liver and onions. Next, I find a way to control this weather.

No sense in exposing myself to the harsh elements all night. No sense in exposing myself at all. Hmm, I wonder if that's still illegal when you're all alone? Probably -- I better not risk it. I've never been a do-it-yourselfer, but I think I'm beginning to get the hang of this survivor lifestyle. Maybe I'll flip this shanty to the next sucker that washes up here.

It was a long and taxing day. No telling what will happen next, but I'm rested and ready for anything. Even though my mind was racing all night, my body has never been so tired. I slept like a baby... cried like one too.

text: I had to come up with a way to manage my trash. I certainly don't want to live in filth. I got my waste management under control -- without involving the Teamsters. This island may be the only place where that's possible. On the other hand, this seems like the perfect place to find Jimmy Hoffa.

Now that I had a place to dispose of trash, I cleaned up the mess on the beach. Okay, trying to keep a jungle beach clean may be a losing proposition, but I do have a lot of free time these days. Maybe later I'll count sand grains for fun, then try to beat that number the next day. Note to self: sarcasm helps less.

I always wanted beachfront property. I might as well try and make the most of what's here. The ocean water looked very inviting, so I went for a dip. I feel like a new person after my swim. I should do that more often. Worst case -- I'll swim home.

An ocean fish would make an excellent meal. I tried to spear one... several times. But I finally caught a fish! It took some time and patience, but I actually speared a wild fish -- a fierce and dangerous sea fish. I have never felt so alive before. I just hope that the fish don't find their own spears.

I cooked the fish I caught on the fire. If the smell attracts any wild animals... I'll eat them too! Who knew that watching countless hours of cooking shows on cable would payoff one day? I wrapped my fish in a leaf and cooked it on the fire. It may be the single most delicious thing I've ever eaten... here.

After taking a closer look at that debris by the water's edge, I think it'll make a good starting point for a raft. Granted, a better starting point for my raft would be SimCity Harbor, but who's complaining?

I combined the fallen bamboo with the flotsam debris to make a raft base. My raft project is officially underway. It feels good to be in control again... even if it is a completely false sense of control. It's the thought that counts, right?
I walked the shoreline and combed the beach for anything useful. I found the exact machete that I wanted for my tenth birthday. Better late then never.
I cleared out the bamboo, hacked a path into the jungle. Now I can explore the island and try to find help -- or a date... hopefully both in one.

Am I the first one to set foot in this jungle? It doesn't seem that way. I found a wrecked plane in the jungle. If the pilot survived the crash, they could still be on the island. I will try to be optimistic... for both of our sakes.
I searched the cockpit of the wreckage for supplies, or better yet, a radio. There was a map of the island inside. It's faint and difficult to read, but at least it's a starting point.

The trek into the jungle was more fruitful than I anticipated. I kept exploring to see what else I could find. I found a family of orangutans and some kind of idol. It looks native, but I guess it could've come from the wreckage or the pilot. I want to know more about the idol. And I want an orangutan.
There was some kind of idol at the base of the orangutans' tree. I went to get a closer look at it. An orangutan beat me up -- badly. I was sucker-punched, and that's all I'm going to say about that.
I gathered some bananas to bribe the fighting orangutans. If this doesn't work, I guess I'll have to learn Judo... or find three other, morally liberal, orangutans to distract these three.

They always said that one can get more flies with honey, than vinegar. Well, "they" sure know their fighting primates. The orangutans loved the banana bribes. I had them eating out of the palm of my hand -- literally.
I thought the idol may hold some clues about the island. I took it from the orangutans. I hope they don't call the cops. What am I thinking? Everyone knows that orangutans hate cops.
After hitting my adventure quota for the day, I returned to camp with the idol. Had I known I would be returning with company, I would have spruced the place up a little.
I wanted to keep the idol close to me. I placed it somewhere nice. It turns out the idol itself was a great way to spruce up the camp.
I took a closer look at this idol. For the first time on this island I'm not all alone. I finally have someone to talk to. Too bad he's the strong, quiet type.

It could take quite some time to finish my raft. I needed an overall food and resource gathering plan. So I planned my survival strategy. Plan your work and work your plan, that's what I always say. Now I have a set schedule for my island job.

One of the orangutans from earlier came to my camp. No banana bribes this time. I won this orangutan over with sheer personality. When it rains it pours... I have two new friends now, Spaulding and an orangutan. This is already a better experience for me than high school.

I thought it'd be nice to have an orangutan around all the time. I adopted it. I can finally strikeout "Pet Primate" from my letters to Santa. Which is good... since I haven't seen any mailboxes here.

It occurred to me that the orangutan could save me a lot of time by gathering food and resources for us both. I explained to the orangutan that it'd have to earn it's own keep around here. The job market is tight right now, but I found it a gig helping me out. I hope it doesn't get a better job offer from a local headhunter.
There has to be something on this island that I can use to tie up the raft base. Between discovering the idol and adopting an orangutan, I almost forgot about my raft. I still need some rope.
I thought the wreckage might have some wires, or something, that I could use as rope. After searching the crashed plane, I found what appears to be Spaulding's missing gem.
I had to see if the jewel fit the idol. Curiosity may have killed the cat, but it gave me a face full of illness. I feel like my insides want to be on the outside. This is not good.

The gas that came out of that idol made me feel terribly ill. If I didn't locate some medicine soon... well, let's not think about that. My luck is finally turning around. I found an old hut with a first aide kit inside. The medicine packed quite a punch, but I feel like my old self again.
I thought there would have to be something to bind my raft base together at the lagoon. I found an old parachute rope in the hut. A phone would've been a nice find, but I'm happy with a rope.
The quicker my raft is finished, the quicker I'll be back home. The parachute rope worked great! I tied up the raft base. It's really starting to come together.
I felt like the lagoon would be a much nicer place to live. Even though I'm still proud of my shelter, I moved into the old hut by the lagoon.
I took some time and resources to fix up the hut by the lagoon. Make it more my own. I added some furnishings. I'm hoping I can get the cover of next month's copy of 'Huts & Jungles' magazine.

text: The idol is the only real clue I have that there may be natives on the island. I wanted to keep it with me. I thought it may be useful as an ice-breaker if I find any islanders. Spaulding and I found some amazing looking ruins in the jungle. There is no doubt that the same people that built these structures also carved the idol, because I had to use the idol to open the doors in the wall. This place is getting very interesting.
After placing the idol on the altar in the ruins, the doors opened! Sadly, I had to leave Spaulding back on the altar. But on the other side of the doors I found more castaways!

I had so many questions. I thought that surely one of these new castaways would be able to shed some light on what exactly happened. I spent some time speaking to each of the other survivors from the Solomon Queen. Not the friendliest bunch considering our circumstances. At this point I'd rather have kept Spaulding. But again, I will try to remain optimistic.

Rhinehart could've been anywhere on the island. I started looking for him right away. Finding a needle in a haystack is nothing compared to finding a professor in a jungle, but I did it. I found Professor Rhinehart!

I met some island natives! Too bad you don't get a second chance at first impressions. I tried to get in good with the locals -- didn't go well at all. It must have been something that I said, or my body language.

Rhinehart looked like the kind of guy that knew a lot of stuff. Unlike the other survivors, Rhinehart seems to have a plan, and the motivation to survive. Although, he does seem a little too happy to be stranded here. Oh well, I guess just waking up in the morning is a gift at that age.

The Professor seemed like my best shot at getting off this island sooner than later. I followed him, trying not to lose him in the thick jungle. We arrived at our destination. I'll say this, The Crossroads is one scary place... especially if you're a ram.
There it was! Rhinehart showed me a pole that I could use as a mast, disguised as a frightening totem. I grabbed one.

I had another piece to add to the raft. I didn't want to waste any time, and the raft is now masted. I wish my high school shop teacher could see it... uh, I mean with his good eye. I still feel really bad about that nail-gun incident.
It was time to get back to the hut by the lagoon. When I returned, the other survivors had made themselves right at home. I was fuming at first, but Rhinehart calmed me down.
This download requires The Sims 2 Update or an expansion pack to be installed.

I had enough food for everyone. So I served the other castaways a meal. I hoped they like island cuisine. I served the other survivors a hut-cooked meal. If this doesn't improve their dispositions, then I don't know what will.

I learned that everyone deserves a second chance at a first impression. I mingled and tried to get to know the others better. It wasn't that bad, but I think I still prefer the company of Spaulding and the orangutans.
I thought that weaving a sail out of grass was a great idea, but first I'd have to find just the right kind of grass to use. I traveled to Scavenger Fields to find the perfect grass.
The tall grass patches looked perfect. I started with those. I cut some grass for a sail. Now I just have to weave it into a sail. Too bad I don't have any idea how to weave a sail out of cut grass.

I saw a little girl in trouble, running from hyenas. I had to do something, but did I really just thwart wild hyenas? Yes, I did! I'm learning so much about myself here. Seriously, I am the last person that would've been picked most likely to save a someone from becoming hors d'oeuvres for hyenas.

Nanihi, the little girl that I saved from the hyenas, invited me back to her village to meet her dad, the chief. This was the first time I'd been invited to meet the chief of anything, much less a native village. There's no way I was passing this invitation up! Of course I accepted. And the village is breath-taking. It is truly beautiful.
Kiri: "Now the only fire I burn is for the trash pit. The wind keeps blowing it out. I am tired of lighting it."
Timoti: "I could tell you the legend of "Tuku Tuzu" over a game of chess. The story may help keep you out of trouble."
Orama: "A bad memory guards my heart, but keeps me from winning what I want most, a Singing Stone from Scavenger Fields."
Emobi: "I can help you find the love you seek. But first, I must repair the broken things. And I am not a quick fixer."

Rarahu let me know that some of the tribe wanted to meet me. I wanted to get to know all of the villagers, and the best way to do that is some quality one-on-one time. Meeting Kiri, Timoti, Emobi and Orama was great! Each one of them gave me a gift. It felt like my birthday and speed-dating wrapped into one. I hope they liked me.
There was more to the village? All of it amazing! The Village Harbor is like a resort spot. It's twice as nice as the brochure for Meet Your Mate!

text: Akolo: "If I had a jar of light, I could gaze at my reflection in the water until sunrise."
Akolo: "If I had a jar of light, I would keep it by my bed at night, to remind me of you."
Rainui: "You can start by pushing me in the swing... if you are strong enough."
Rainui: "You can start by pushing me in the swing... it is great for flabby triceps."
Ahio: "I spend many hours standing in this ocean, spear in hand, sun beating down and rarely do I have fish to show for it."
Tumata: "I wish everyone could hear the music you have put in my heart, but I do not play an instrument."
Tumata: "I wish everyone could hear the music in my heart, but I do not play an instrument."
Everyone here has been so nice and hospitable. I met more great islanders and received more wonderful gifts in the Village Harbor. I count Rainui, Tumata, Akolo and Ahio all as friends now.

The Chief wanted to meet me. I felt like an ambassador.Meeting Chief Manave was the highlight of my visit to the village. And that's saying a lot because the entire experience was jammed-packed with highlight reel moments.

I had never felt so at ease around new people before. The Chief invited me to the Volcano Festival at the Hot Springs. I accepted. This place is the ultimate R and R spot. If I can't unwind here, then I'm wound tighter than humanly possible.

As the honored guest, I was asked to choose a date for the festival. I thought I should picked someone that I really like. For all I know going on a "date" here could mean that I wake up married. I hope my date likes me... I mean, likes me likes me.
I didn't want $NeighborLocal:2 to get bored, so I improvised. We got a chance to play with each other a little. Playing with $NeighborLocal:2 is fun!

From the way the Chief and Huhana greeted me, it seems like hugging would be a mild greeting here. I didn't want $NeighborLocal:2 to think that I was being too forward. After hugging my date, I realized that I need physical contact with others just as much as food for survival.

I never wanted the date to end. I wondered if $NeighborLocal:2 was ready to take it to the next level. We cuddled together. You know, I've been grooming my orangutan alone for so long that I almost forgot what it was like to cuddle with a date.

The natives wanted me to live among them. That's a big decision. I went back to the hut, to find a quiet place to think about the Chief's offer. All I wanted was a little peace and quiet, instead I come home to uninvited guests -- Hugh and his gang. They're noisy, rude, ungrateful, annoying, jerk-face, party-of-one crashers! I feel like Hugh is bungee-jumping from space, secured by his ankles to my last nerve.

That was it! I gave that Hugh Bailey character a piece of my mind. I confronted him about his behavior, attitude, and selfishness. It was a total waste of energy and time. He's hopeless. I need to be surrounded by positivity right now.

I needed to tell the Professor what was going on and where he could find me. I feel bad leaving Rhinehart alone with these people, but he doesn't seem to mind taking care of them. He must be an incredibly patient man. I told him where he can find me. Let's hope he keeps that info to himself.

It was time to move on. I had bigger and better things on the horizon. The hut that the villagers gave me looks just like one of the pictures from Club Meet Your Mate. I should've moved here a long time ago. This is the coolest house I've ever seen, much less owned!

With all the excitement lately, I had almost forgotten about my raft. I hoisted the woven grass sail that Huhana made for me. The raft is looking good, but I should take my time and do it right. No need to rush it. Besides, I hate my job back in the city.

Abandoned village? Curse? Shaman? This just kept getting better. The Chief sent me to talk the tribe's ex-communicated Shaman in Creepy Hollow. The place lives up to the name. Can't wait to meet the decorator... he'll probably want to make a skin-suit out of me.

I hated to interrupt, but it didn't look like I had a choice. That Shaman was meditating like it was his job. After speaking with the him, I realized that all the fuss was about my old buddy, Spaulding. I knew there was something special about that idol. I'm a great judge of the personified character.
I remembered exactly where I last saw the idol. I hoped it's still there -- it wasn't. I found Spaulding back with the orangutans in Simian City. Maybe I'll open a lost and found hut.

I returned to Creepy Hollow. That Shaman is one neat guy, but just an okay kisser. He couldn't believe that I found the missing idol. The Shaman told me what I need to do in order to get past the jaguar guarding the Forbidden Village -- find a leaf in a jungle.

I was off to find a leaf in the jungle. I picked a Nepeta leaf for Mata. At least, I'm pretty sure it's the right leaf. I'll find out soon enough. I mean, for all I know I just garnished myself with jaguar parsley.

I needed to relax. If cats can sense fear, then this one should've been on sensory overload as I approached. The leaf worked like a charm -- a herbal charm. Mata turned out to be a total pussycat. Now I can finally get into the cursed Forbidden Village. What am I thinking?

Tame jaguar guardian -- check. Travel to the cursed forbidden village -- check. Entering the Forbidden Village, it dawned on me how many villagers must have lost their lives here. This place fills me with a deep sadness and sense of loss. I can't imagine how the tribe must feel.
All things considered, finding this drum should've been a cake walk. But the Forbidden Village turned out to be haunted by the ghosts of fallen villagers. I want to help these ghosts find peace.

I needed to put the urns left behind by the ghosts with the others. The ghosts' urns were never placed on the proper altar. I helped the ghosts find peace by moving their urns to the right spot. Now they will let me take the drum.
It was back to my new gig as a drum delivery service. I got the drum. It was right where the Chief said it'd be (minus the ghosts).
This was the fun part. I made the Chief's day, reuniting him with his drum. He's so happy that he's throwing the first luau since the curse to celebrate.
I have never been one to miss a party. The luau is in full swing. This tribe sure knows how to party!
There was $NeighborLocal:2! I thought that a kiss would be a fair trade for a party drum. I tried to steal a kiss, but $NeighborLocal:2 is playing hard to get.
I'd do whatever it took to impress $NeighborLocal:2. At first, drinking the volcano water was like gargling with lava, but it turned out to be rather good.
It was Limbo time! How low did I go? Let's just say that my athletic prowess shined through again on the limbo pole -- meaning I didn't break any bones. Good times!

Talk about getting raked across the coals... $NeighborLocal:2 wanted me to walk across hot coals -- for fun! That's right, I walked across fire! I am a fire-walker! I can't believe I just did that. Walking across hot coals is something I never would have had the courage to try back in the city.

It was time to make my move, again. $NeighborLocal:2 and I shared our first kiss. It was life changing. I never want to kiss anyone else again. No doubt about it, I'm in love -- and I'm getting in deep!

The Chief gave me a rudder for my raft. The raft has been the last thing on my mind lately. $NeighborLocal:2 didn't take the idea of me leaving well at all. I'm not so sure how I feel about anymore either. I went back to my hut to sulk.

I awoke with a clear head. A sound sleep was just what I needed. I dreamt I was back in the city -- at work in an office job. Then, the dream changed and I was locked in a cage at a zoo, then drowning in a rich man's aquarium. It was a nightmare! My life is here now.

I needed to find $NeighborLocal:2 and say that I'm staying on the island. I found $NeighborLocal:2 in the jungle, sick with the same illness that the idol gave me. I can't help but feel that this is somehow all my fault.
I had to talk to $NeighborLocal:2. I told $NeighborLocal:2 that I'm not going to leave the island. I just hope it's not too little, too late.
In order to prove to the Chief that the "curse" can be cured, I kissed $NeighborLocal:2. Fortunately, I was right and I didn't get sick. I will not allow that to be the last time our lips meet.
I needed to get back to the raft before any more villagers got sick. A flaming projectile from the volcano struck my raft. The woven grass sail is burnt and useless. I don't know what to do next.

Rhinehart told me about an abandoned research base on the island. He thinks I may be able to find a replacement sail there. Please let the Professor be right! Off I went. At the base I found an old parachute that I can use as a new sail. There's something very fishy about this place though. I have a feeling Rhinehart knows more than he's been telling me.
I hustled back to the raft to install the new sail. The old parachute worked perfect as a replacement! My raft is finally finished!
I set sail with my heart in my stomach. The raft worked! It stayed afloat and that's all it needed to do in my opinion.
It looked like I'd have to find my own way around the island. The directions Rhinehart gave me around Volcano Island were out of date. I had to find a new way. Turning back is not an option.
I hoped the staff was the only thing living in that hollow tree. It was. I found the Staff of Tuzu exactly where Rhinehart's "legend" said it'd be.
This didn't look good. Again, I was forced to find my own way around the island. A volcanic tremor blocked my old path.

I found another survivor from the Solomon Queen, Bart Pittman. This guy was in pretty rough shape. I doubted I'd be able to help him, but at least I could keep him company for a bit. He died right in front of me, but not before he implicated a "professor" in sabotaging the Queen. I have a bad feeling that Rhinehart is responsible for the shipwreck.
I sailed, paddled and pushed the raft back to the main island as quickly as I could. When I returned to the Village Harbor, I could see that the disease had been spreading.
I had to find a cure. I had to open the temple. Rhinehart was waiting for me at the House of Tuzu.

I wanted to find out what game Rhinehart had been playing with me. I confronted Rhinehart about what Pittman told me. He showed his true colors. The nice, old mentor figure is actually pure evil incarnate. No wonder he didn't mind living with Hugh.

Could I trust Rhinehart? I didn't have a choice. I had to try to save $NeighborLocal:2 and the others. Rhinehart told me how to use the staff to open the temple. I should have known there wouldn't be a cure inside. Instead, the temple was filled with treasure and Tuku Tuzu's youth potion. I saw Rhinehart grow younger after drinking from the Chalice of Days.

All this time Rhinehart was just using me -- and all the others. I couldn't let him get away with that. It was time for the evil Professor Rhinehart to receive his comeuppance. I used the Staff of Tuzu to give Rhinehart exactly what he deserved.
I'd have to go back to the Village Harbor without a cure. I returned to the Village Harbor with my heart weighing heavy. I felt like I had let everyone down.

I'd try anything to save $NeighborLocal:2! The Staff of Tuzu held the cure for the temple's curse. I used the staff to heal $NeighborLocal:2, to my surprise the rest of the villagers were healed as well. Maybe true love really can conquer all.
Well, I popped the big question to $NeighborLocal:2, only to be interrupted by Hugh Bailey.
I had to find out what that crazy old man had been up to! I accepted Rhinehart's shipment. It was a weather control device!

Now it was time to set off on the biggest adventure of my life -- starting a family with $NeighborLocal:2. I planned a vacation around trying to meet my soulmate, got shipwrecked, had many adventures, made new friends, and ultimately found exactly what I was seeking. Life is funny. Some people deserve what they get. Others get what they deserve. You wouldn't think there would be much of a difference between the two -- but there is. I think the trick is never knowing which type of person you are.

Sailing the world on the crew of a luxury yacht has been rewarding, but lonely. Could that be about to change? The captain just announced that the ship is heading for shore leave at Meet Your Mate -- the hottest singles resort in the world! This is a once in a lifetime opportunity to meet the love of your life.

Yesterday you were trapped in the daily grind back in Sim City. Today you're on your way to the hottest singles resort in the world to do a story for 'Going Places' magazine. It's a once in a lifetime opportunity, and not just for your writing career. Somewhere out there you're determined to find your own special someone.

Looking for a way to say “I love you”? Look no further than Delarosa Flowers. Florence’s arrangements are almost as famous as her delicious pasta dishes. The secret to her sauce? Rose-hips!

The Jacquets left everything they had behind and tried to build a new life in Bluewater Village. Will they go from rags to riches and create a healthy franchise system that goes public? Or will they fail and watch their dreams crumble like a week old croissant?
Wanda and Stephen hoped their toy shop would be in the family for generations to come, but their daughter seems to have other plans. Can Melody follow her own dreams and still keep her parents happy?

Checo and Lisa Ramirez have worked hard to get their furniture store off the ground. Though salesmanship has always come easy to Checo, running a business has its own challenges. Now that their daughter Tessa is in school, they can concentrate fully on making their business the best.

Ruthless. Cunning. Brilliant. Ridiculously wealthy. These are just a few words the locals use to describe the Landgraab Family, whose entrepreneurial ambitions can’t be stopped by anything but their own mistakes. When you have this much money, you're your own worst enemy.
Come enjoy an exciting new shopping and entertainment destination! If you're looking to update your closet, your image or your family room, Bluewater Village will have something for you.

Are you tired of using the same roof slope as the neighbors? Want to spruce up your house? Simultaneously press Ctrl + Shift + C to open the command console. Then enter roofSlopeAngle and a number (15-75) to determine the angle of your roof. The simple changes will bring you one step closer to the dream home you’ve always wanted!

Have you fallen in love with the new Underwater and Fantasy themed furniture sets, but hate sorting through the Buy Catalog to find the objects? Quicken your search by using the Collections feature, which can be found in the sort section of the control panel, just below the room sort. Collections do the sorting for you, because shopping should be about buying, not searching!

Many Sims have relocated to the quiet, comfortable countryside, in the hopes that life and family can firmly plant their roots in the middle of nowhere.
Fresh crops aren’t the only thing growing in the farming community of Riverblossom Hills – love is in the air and many a relationship is on the verge of blossoming.  Unfortunately, problems are bound to sprout in a town this small.
Things are looking up, but hearts can always turn cold with the onset of winter.

Jason gave up his name and changed his lifestyle for the love of his green-skinned goddess.  Despite the love that they share will they be able to raise a happy, healthy child?  Can Rose adjust to living in a town instead of the great outdoors?
Leod McGreggor has a farm... and an orchard.  Will he be so focused on gardening that he forgets to cultivate friendships?

After his wife left to become a Dread Pirate, it took Gabe a long time to trust again.  Is his relationship with Patricia meant to last? Will Patricia and Jules be able to work out their problems and realize how similar they really are?

Patricia and Cleo moved to town when Cleo's aunt, Catherine, offered Cleo her old home - which they just finished remodelling.  Will they find excitement in this quiet town after the dust has cleared?  Will Patricia and Gabe make a life together?

Can Catherine and Betty cope with the loss of their close friend and face their own imminent mortality or will they find a way to cheat death?  Will Andrew and Jacob find a way to fulfill their dreams in the great game of life?
Having recently moved to Riverblossom Hills has had a wonderful effect on the Roth's!  Sandra and Xander are doing great in school, Morty found a great job, but Stella seems a bit restless...

text: Gentrific "Way of the Wood" Mantel Fireplace

What is it about a roaring fire that's so magical? The warmth of the flames? The sounds of crackling wood? The smell of smoke and soot? Soak in all these primal pleasures with this handsome mantel fireplace, guaranteed to put a warm spell on a cold evening.
Shiny Things, INC. "Estomago" Pot Belly Stove

Deep in the Appalachian wilderness, a government agent burst through the doors of what was thought to be an illegal moonshine still. What he discovered was an authentic pot belly stove factory that had been in operation for 159 years! ShinyThings, INC. snapped up these heat-radiating beauties, modernized the log cabin factory, and the rest was history.

Enjoy the hearty glow of fiery logs made of sawdust and glue with the Red Ember freestanding fireplace. It adds surprising warmth and good cheer to any living space with a hole drilled in the ceiling. A conical stack swiftly clears smoke and ash from the hearth bed and deposits them somewhere else.

Watch the embers glow and the flames dance, while your Sims heat their entire house and help the environment too. The Flame-O-Rama's vintage turn-of-the-century styling recalls the days when a fireplace was a necessity, not an amenity. It's the perfect place to warm up and mellow out during your Sims' next power outage!
Casbah Casuals Fireplace by 40 Thieves Ltd.

Warm the cockles of your Sim's heart with the Casbah Casuals Fireplace by 40 Thieves Ltd. The carved stone face, etched wood trim, and mosaic mantlepiece are sure to give your Sim's home a rich, exotic look and feel.

Breathing new life into an ancient form, Modern Primitive's Ignito Fireplace makes a bold and modern statement. A statement like "Hey, look at the fire I made! It’s not any kind of old style fire! It’s a modern, up to date fire that says lots of things about me and my lifestyle choices! Yeah! Shed light, warm backsides, but don’t be fooled! This isn’t your grandfather’s fireplace...it’s way more rectilinear and stuff.

Hard times? Down on your luck? You, fair Sim, are in luck now! This Shoddy Fireplace was designed from the rusted bottom upwards to remind you of one thing -- it could be worse! Just imagine if the Shoddy Fireplace was all you had for warmth, your only possession. Yes indeed, it could be worse, and it could be yours, now, for just a few Simoleons!

text: Sloppy|With their constant disregard of cleanliness and hygiene, sloppy Sims are content to simply "be."  They tend to enjoy just about anything that doesn't require planning or cleaning up on their part.|||0xcb980e90

text: Neat|Tidy Sims typically enjoy cleaning up the house or grooming themselves in front of a mirror. There's always something to be done around the house and they'll more often than not be found doing it; great for a house, but it can tire Sims out.|||0xcb980e90

Shy|Introspective and quiet, shy Sims often think about the world around them and write in their diaries rather than actually interact with anyone.  It may be harder to break out of their shells, but if shy Sims take the time to get to know others they'll be delighted by the social world awaiting them.|||0xcb980e90

Outgoing|Outgoing Sims are likely to jump headfirst into any situation.  Charm and confidence are their best traits and when they're in a friendly mood they enjoy group activities most of all. Keep an eye on these characters, though; outgoing Sims can be too brash, and others aren't always so impressed.|||0xcb980e90

Grouchy|Grouchy Sims, despite their sour mood, can still be social creatures. They'll probably enjoy teasing a Sim as much as telling a joke.  They don't seem to mind when other Sims overreact and they like playing a game as much as anyone else, but be warned: they tend to be sore losers.|||0xcb980e90

text: Nice|Encouraging and generous, nice Sims tend to be easy to get along with and very positive.  They'll listen to what other Sims have to say whether it's interesting or not and clean up after dirty roommates. If they don't watch out though, other Sims may take advantage of their good nature.|||0xcb980e90

Lazy|Lazy Sims have been known to veg out on the couch for hours on end, so naturally, they don't need much sleep to sustain their constant lazing. They still enjoy socializing with other Sims and can be persuaded to get out of the house once in awhile.|||0xcb980e90

text: Active|Active Sims are almost always on the move but need a lot of food and sleep to keep up their hectic pace. They're apt to be happiest while breaking a sweat, an exhausting idea to most other Sims.  An active Sim will usually get more enjoyment from watching sports on TV than reading a book.|||0xcb980e90

Serious|Quiet, thoughtful Sims are more inclined to enjoy logic puzzles and good conversation, but they don't respond too well to chaos or silly behavior. Repairing broken items or working on an important project can keep serious Sims content.|||0xcb980e90

Playful|Playful Sims are more likely to find entertainment and fun in the world around them; they tend to be more curious than any other Sim. They may have a lighthearted nature, but they can wear themselves out with their antics, as well as get on their fellow Sim's nerves.|||0xcb980e90

Genius|Genius pets tend to catch on much faster, which is obvious when training. This is a good trait for career-minded pets to have and is also ideal for those interested in a more obedient, reliable animal.|||0xcb980e90
Doofus|Doofus pets are somewhat dimwitted, so training may take a bit longer. Pets with this trait may not notice things happening around them and they tend to be a bit slow to react.|||0xcb980e90

Hyper|Hyper pets are full of energy and are always more inclined to play. These pets will spend much less time loafing around and will take the time to interact with everything around them.|||0xcb980e90
Lazy|Lazy pets can often be found resting happily when and wherever the mood strikes them. Sleep is their highest priority, so they may not always be willing to play.|||0xcb980e90
Independent|Independent pets don't necessarily require (or tolerate) the constant attention of a companion. These pets often react indifferently to playful or affectionate interactions.|||0xcb980e90
Friendly|Friendly pets are always quick to greet with a warm welcome. These affectionate pets, often inclined to play with others, really are a Sim's best friend.|||0xcb980e90
Aggressive|Aggressive pets will often growl or hiss first, and ask questions later. Always on the defensive, it isn't wise to tamper with "their" things or push them around.|||0xcb980e90
Cowardly|Cowardly pets are not interested in fighting or standing their ground. When the fur begins to fly, these pets can usually be seen scurrying in the opposite direction.|||0xcb980e90

Pigpen|Pigpen pets shudder at the thought of leaving a good dirt or trash pile alone. Less than concerned about cleanliness, these pets may cause discomfort for those with sensitive noses.|||0xcb980e90
Finicky|Finicky pets maintain high standards and will rarely be seen with a hair out of place. Furthermore, don't expect them to tolerate a dirty or cheap food bowl.|||0xcb980e90

Welcome to The Sims 2 Nightlife! The Sims of %s just can't wait to get Downtown and start partying, but before they can do that, you need to associate a Downtown neighborhood with %s! Do you want to do this now?

It's time to make a nightlife destination for %s! Select "Downtown" above and press the Play button if you'd like to use the default neighborhood.

There's all kinds of new Sims to meet, and even a few spooky surprises... so don't just sit there, buy your Sims a car and get them cruising on down to downtown so they can get the party started!  Downtown is the new hot spot where your Sims can cut loose and party all night!!  Food-loving Sims can find great dining, and there's some great dance spots for Sims who love to boogie down. If your Sims want to sing their hearts out, why not drop by a karaoke bar?  And if family fun is what you're looking for, head for a bowling alley and start throwing those strikes!!  Your Sims can even get themselves some great rewards just for going on dream dates and going out with friends.

Hyper|Hyper pets are full of energy and are always more inclined to play. These pets will spend much less time loafing around and will take the time to interact with everything around them.|||0x4906501e
Lazy|Lazy pets can often be found resting happily when and wherever the mood strikes them. Sleep is their highest priority, so they may not always be willing to play.|||0x4906501e
Independent|Independent pets don't necessarily require (or tolerate) the constant attention of a companion. These pets often react indifferently to playful or affectionate interactions.|||0x4906501e

Social|Sims are friendly creatures that crave social interaction -- the only problem is there aren't that many around. Sims can write in a diary or write letters home to ease the loneliness; and can hold a conversation with a surprising number of things in a pinch. To fulfill your Sims social need press L. |0xab201576|0xab201593|0x4906500d

Bladder|When a Sim's gotta go, a Sim's gotta go. And there's really only one solution to that kind of problem-get them to an appropriate bush or toilet as fast as possible. To have your Sim relieve themselves press B. |0xab201579|0xab201581|0x4906500d

Environment|Decorations and landscaping around the lot will affect the environment. Sims like bright, clean spaces with plenty of color and light. A nice dwelling with well kept surroundings will surely fulfill this need. To have your Sim clean press K. |0xab201578|0xab201594|0x4906500d

Family|There's nothing like the bonds of family to make a Sim feel happy inside. Giving hugs and talking to relatives will boost this need and strengthen relationships. |0xab201592|0xab201587|0x4906500d
Hunger|All animals, like Sims, need to eat. Hyenas and jaguars will usually leave the lot to hunt and come back when full, while orangutans primarliy eat fruit. |0xFeed8c11|0|0xfeed2001
Energy|Few things will energize a pet like a long slumber on the ground, except even more of the same. |0xFeed8c07|0|0xfeed2001
Comfort|Animals love to be comfortable and will certainly lie on the ground to ease their aching muscles. |0xFeed8c05|0|0xfeed2001
Fun|Animals enjoy breaks filled with fun and games just like Sims. Teach them to fetch, play finger wiggle or encourage them to play with others when they need a boost of Fun. |Feed8c09|0|0xfeed2001

Hygiene|Animals will become rather stinky over time, especially with a house full of things to play with. Jaguars will clean themselves and so will orangutans, though your Sims will need to bathe hyenas...which isn't always going to be easy. |0xFeed8c13|0|0xfeed2001
Social|Animals require frequent attention from their masters to stay happy. Sims should train them and encourage playfulness to maximize a pet's social well-being. |0xFeed8c17|0|0xfeed2001

Love|PlantSims are friendly creatures that crave social interaction. They can fulfill their needs by interacting with friends, family, and neighbors. The telephone is a great way for Sims to invite people over or to catch up on the latest gossip.|dafe8100|dafe8101|0x4906500d
Sunlight|PlantSims cannot grow and stay healthy without a heavy dosage of sunlight to keep them warm! Bask in the sun's rays outdoors or enjoy the glow of the sun lamp.|dafe8102|dafe8103|0x4906500d

Neat|Tidy Sims typically enjoy cleaning up the house or grooming themselves in front of a mirror. There's always something to be done around the living space and they'll more often than not be found doing it; great for the living space, but it can tire Sims out.|||0x4906501e

Sloppy|With their constant disregard of cleanliness and hygiene, sloppy Sims are content to simply "be." They tend to enjoy just about anything that doesn't require planning or cleaning up on their part.|||0x4906501e

Outgoing|Outgoing Sims are likely to jump headfirst into any situation. Charm and confidence are their best traits and when they're in a friendly mood they enjoy group activities most of all. Keep an eye on these characters, though; outgoing Sims can be too brash, and others aren't always so impressed.|||0x4906501e

Shy|Introspective and quiet, shy Sims often think about the world around them and write in their diaries rather than actually interact with anyone. It may be harder for them to break out of their shells, but when shy Sims take the time to get to know others they're delighted by the social world awaiting them.|||0x4906501e

Active|Active Sims are almost always on the move but need a lot of food and sleep to keep up their hectic pace. They're apt to be happiest while breaking a sweat, an exhausting idea to most other Sims. An active Sim will usually get more enjoyment from swimming than from writing in a diary.|||0x4906501e

Lazy|Lazy Sims can easily veg out for hours on end, so naturally, they don't need as much sleep to sustain their constant lazing. They still enjoy socializing with other Sims and can be persuaded to get out of the house once in awhile.|||0x4906501e

Playful|Playful Sims are more likely to find entertainment and fun in the world around them; they tend to be more curious than other Sims. They have a lighthearted nature, but they can wear themselves out with their antics, as well as get on their fellow Sim's nerves.|||0x4906501e

Serious|Quiet, thoughtful Sims are inclined to enjoy logic puzzles and good conversation, but they don't respond too well to chaos or silly behavior. Repairing broken items or working on an important project can keep a serious Sim content.|||0x4906501e

Nice|Encouraging and generous, nice Sims tend to be easy to get along with and very positive. They'll listen to what other Sims have to say whether it's interesting or not, and are willing to clean up after others. But if they don't watch out, other Sims may take advantage of them.|||0x4906501e

Sims with the Family Aspiration long to be part of a big, happy family. They need "Quality Time" with family members, and lots of meaningful interactions with all the branches of their family tree.
Sims with the Popularity Aspiration desire flocks of friends and killer parties, so if they aren't on the shell phone, practicing politics, or dancin' the night away, they probably should be.

Sims with the Fortune Aspiration crave resources, rising to the top of their careers, and just plain expensive stuff. They'll need all of these things in spades to keep their materialistic minded lives long and happy.

Sims with the Knowledge Aspiration want to know everything there is to know about anything. Make sure they have the time to study and explore every nook and cranny. Their lives are a simple equation: the more Knowledge, and the longer and brainier the life.

Sims with the Romance Aspiration crave lots of lovin' with as many different Sims as they can find, so setting aside the time for them to chase those hot prospects is key. Fill their lives with hot steamy nights and lust-filled days in order to keep Romance Sims' lives long and exciting.

All Sims have the Grow Up Aspiration when they're young, and they all need the same thing: love, time and attention from their family. See to it the other Sims around them make the time to teach these young'uns what they need to learn, and you'll give them a great head start on life.
